schema_grounding_notes: phenotype_name: use the official HPO term name — e.g. 'Seizure' not 'seizures', 'Intellectual disability' not 'mental retardation'
aspect: P=Phenotypic abnormality (264207 rows), C=Clinical course (8444 rows), I=Inheritance/Mode of inheritance (9104 rows), H=Past medical history (124 rows), M=Clinical modifier (78 rows)
frequency in disease_phenotype_annotation_hpo is a raw fraction (e.g. '7/42') or HP frequency term (e.g. HP:0040282); NOT an enum
frequency in gene_phenotype_association_hpo is a raw fraction string or HP term; filter by numeric range is not directly supported
qualifier: reserved for the value 'NOT' (phenotype explicitly absent), but in this snapshot the column is null in 100% of served rows — no 'NOT' values are present
onset: HP ontology term (e.g. HP:0003593) or free text age-of-onset string

source (gene_disease_association_hpo): stored as a full provenance URL, not a friendly label. There are exactly two values — Orphanet rows contain 'orphadata' (http://www.orphadata.org/data/xml/en_product6.xml) and OMIM/MedGen rows contain 'mim2gene' (ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/DATA/mim2gene_medgen). When the user names a source, filter source by the URL substring: 'Orphanet' -> 'orphadata', 'OMIM'/'MedGen' -> 'mim2gene'.

co_output_rules.reason: HPO term names are not unique across versions; include phenotype_id (HP:XXXXXXX) for unambiguous reference
opaque HP:XXXXXXX IDs need the human-readable phenotype name
disease IDs (OMIM/ORPHA) need the human-readable disease name

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What HPO phenotypes are caused by FGFR3 mutations?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: gene→phenotype direct query: gene_symbol (WHERE filter on FGFR3), phenotype_name + phenotype_id (SELECT output, always co-output per co_output_rules). disease_name is IRRELEVANT — the question asks for phenotypes directly linked to the gene, not via disease.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What are the HPO terms for achondroplasia?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: disease→phenotype query: disease_name (WHERE filter on achondroplasia), phenotype_name + phenotype_id (SELECT output). gene_symbol is IRRELEVANT — this is a disease-to-phenotype mapping, not a gene query. Frequency and onset are useful clinical co-outputs.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What genes cause short stature?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: phenotype→gene query: phenotype_name (WHERE filter on 'Short stature'), gene_symbol (SELECT output). disease_name is IRRELEVANT — the question is about which genes are linked to the phenotype, not about diseases. Do NOT add disease_name even if disease_id appears in the join path.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What diseases have the HPO term HP:0001250 (seizures)?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: phenotype→disease query: phenotype_id/phenotype_name (WHERE filter on HP:0001250/Seizure), disease_name + disease_id (SELECT output). gene_symbol is IRRELEVANT — the question asks which diseases are annotated with this phenotype, not which genes cause it.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: What is the definition of HP:0001250?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: HPO term lookup: phenotype_id (WHERE filter on HP:0001250), phenotype_name + definition (SELECT output from phenotype_master_table_hpo). gene_symbol and disease_name are IRRELEVANT — this is a pure ontology term definition lookup, not an association query.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which phenotypes are associated with heterozygous mutations of the BSCL2 gene?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: gene→disease query (mutations context): despite 'phenotypes' in the question, the expected answers are DISEASE NAMES (e.g. Silver syndrome, CMT2, distal HMN type V). Use gene_disease_association_hpo (output: disease_name, association_type). Use gene_phenotype_association_hpo ONLY when the question explicitly asks for HP: codes or specific HP phenotype term names — NOT when 'mutations of gene X' implies disease entities.

filter_few_shot_examples.question: Which amino acid is implicated in Blue diaper syndrome?
filter_few_shot_examples.note: disease→phenotype query about a specific biochemical/metabolite abnormality: disease_name (WHERE filter on Blue diaper syndrome), phenotype_name + phenotype_id (SELECT output from disease_phenotype_association_hpo). The 'amino acid' in the question refers to a phenotype term (e.g. HP:0004365 Abnormal circulating tryptophan concentration). Always route amino-acid/metabolite/biochemical questions about a disease to disease_phenotype_association_hpo — NEVER stop at disease_master_table_hpo alone.

column_notes_override.disease_name: Orphanet or OMIM disease name as stored; e.g. 'Marfan syndrome', 'Phenylketonuria'
column_notes_override.phenotype_name: official HPO term name; do not use lay terms or synonyms as filter values
